title: Best LORR (Law & Order Record Retrieval) Alternatives for 2026
summary: Compare the best LORR (Law & Order Record Retrieval) alternatives for 2026, including Codes Health's nationwide retrieval, human-verified AI insights, and flat-fee pricing.
body_markdown:
When you're weighing LORR alternatives, the decision usually comes down to geographic reach, case volume, and whether you need AI-powered medical analysis on top of document collection. LORR has built a strong reputation with Texas law firms, but many personal injury and mass tort practices handle treatment across state lines and want litigation-focused insights alongside retrieval. This guide covers the top LORR alternatives, and why Codes Health stands out by pairing retrieval with human-verified AI insights, including potential breach-of-care flags, pre-existing condition identification, and future medical expense information for attorney review.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Codes Health stands out as a leading LORR alternative, with litigation-focused AI that flags potential breach-of-care issues, identifies pre-existing conditions, and extracts future medical expense information, with insights verified by humans


-


LORR emphasizes serving Texas law firms; firms handling out-of-state treatment should confirm its provider coverage


-


Codes Health's position is that services promising same-day retrieval often return only the records immediately available, which requires added client involvement to fill the gaps and can contribute to churn. Ask whether a timeline covers initial electronic records or the full requested record set


-


General AI tools like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review, and AI-generated analysis needs verification against source records


-


Advertised base rates don't always reflect the full invoice, so compare the service fee, provider charges, and optional services when requesting quotes


## **What Is LORR and Why Firms Seek Alternatives**


Law & Order Record Retrieval (LORR) is a litigation support provider focused on Texas law firms, offering medical record retrieval alongside court reporting, videography, process service, and trial exhibits. LORR lists offices in San Antonio, Dallas-Fort Worth, and Houston, with Austin-area production handled through San Antonio.


**LORR service offerings:**


-


Medical record retrieval, with requests and notices sent within 24 hours


-


Legal videography and photography


-


Trial exhibits and visual presentation aids


-


Citation and subpoena services


-


Court reporters for depositions


**Common reasons firms explore alternatives:**


-


Multi-state cases: firms with out-of-state treatment want to confirm nationwide provider coverage


-


Analysis needs: interest in potential breach-of-care flags and medical insights alongside retrieval


-


Scalability: mass tort and high-volume practices want automated workflows


LORR testimonials describe long-term relationships with Texas attorneys who praise its efficient, accurate service. For Texas-focused firms that want full litigation support, including videography and trial exhibits, LORR offers comprehensive local service. Firms with multi-state caseloads or a need for AI-powered medical analysis may want to compare the options below.


## **1. Codes Health**


Codes Health goes beyond document collection to deliver litigation-focused insights. Its AI platform extracts the medical details plaintiff attorneys need, including potential breach-of-care indicators, pre-existing conditions, and documented future expenses, with insights verified by humans.


### **Platform Features**


-


Potential breach-of-care flags in medical documentation for attorney review


-


Pre-existing condition identification, cross-referencing patient history across retrieved records


-


Extraction of documented future medical expense information for demand preparation and attorney review


-


Missing Record Review that compares delivered materials against original requests and patient history to help identify gaps


-

-

-


Nationwide retrieval through claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone


-


Custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software for high-volume firms


Authorization pre-validation matters more than it might seem. Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can force a resubmission and put a request back at the start of the provider's response window. Under the[30-day federal standard](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/how-timely-must-a-covered-entity-be/index.html) for HIPAA access requests, providers generally have 30 calendar days to act, and state timelines vary. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


### **Market Position**


Codes Health functions as a[pre-litigation department](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) without the overhead. It describes retrieval timelines of a couple of weeks and offers Missing Record Review to help identify gaps; timing depends on the request and provider response.


Codes Health reports reduced manual review time and increased case capacity for clients by automating paralegal workflows. These are company-reported results, and individual results may vary.


Through the[Filevine partnership](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/filevine-partners-with-codes-health-to-bring-ai-native-medical-record-retrieval-to-legal-teams-302823827.html) announced on July 13, 2026, legal teams can submit requests, track status, communicate with the Codes Health team, and receive completed records without leaving Filevine.


Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, so the platform keeps evolving, improving, and becoming more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices.


### **Pricing**


Flat fee. Confirm included services and any external charges in the engagement terms.


### **Best For**


-


Plaintiff firms with multi-state cases


-


Firms wanting AI-powered analysis with human verification


-


Practices looking to reduce paralegal review time


-


High-volume firms needing custom integrations

## **The Bottom Line**


Most retrieval problems in multi-state personal injury and mass tort cases are preventable: authorizations rejected over a missing signature or date, out-of-state providers that never get the right request, and gaps that surface only once trial prep is underway. A faster first delivery doesn't fix those, and a partial record set can push the follow-up work back onto your team and your clients.


What prevents those failures is validating requests before submission, following up across every channel until providers respond, and checking for gaps before the file closes. Codes Health builds those steps into one workflow, then adds human-verified AI insights on potential breach-of-care issues, pre-existing conditions, and future expenses for attorney review. For firms ready to move beyond basic document retrieval,[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) offers a flat fee alternative built for modern legal practices.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What's the best LORR alternative for firms with multi-state cases?**


For firms handling treatment across multiple states, Codes Health provides nationwide retrieval through claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone, along with AI-powered analysis and Missing Record Review to help identify gaps. LORR emphasizes serving Texas law firms, so firms with out-of-state treatment should confirm its provider coverage.


### **How does AI-powered retrieval differ from traditional services?**


Retrieval services collect and deliver documents, and analysis capabilities vary by provider. AI-powered platforms like Codes Health extract litigation-focused insights, such as potential breach-of-care indicators, pre-existing conditions, and future medical expense information, with insights verified by humans. Codes Health reports reduced manual review time for clients (company-reported; individual results may vary).


### **Can same-day retrieval services deliver complete medical records?**


Same-day speed usually refers to sending requests or receiving initial electronic records, not necessarily the full requested record set. Codes Health's position is that services promising same-day retrieval often return only the records immediately available, which requires added client involvement and can contribute to churn. Codes Health describes retrieval timelines of a couple of weeks and uses Missing Record Review to help identify gaps before documentation is marked complete. When comparing services, ask whether client participation is required.


### **Why can't general AI tools like ChatGPT analyze medical records for litigation?**


General-purpose AI tools like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review. AI-generated medical record analysis requires verification against source records, consistent with[ABA ethics guidance](https://www.americanbar.org/news/abanews/aba-news-archives/2024/07/aba-issues-first-ethics-guidance-ai-tools/) , so firms should evaluate accuracy, confidentiality protections, source traceability, and human review. Codes Health's platform is purpose-built to analyze medical records with high precision for plaintiff firms, with AI-generated insights verified by humans.


### **What integrations does Codes Health support?**


Codes Health partners with Filevine for native case management integration, letting firms submit requests, track status, communicate with the team, and receive records without leaving their case files. For high-volume customers, Codes Health builds custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software.
